name: The Upper House
positioning: Design-led luxury hotel by architect Andre Fu, set high above Pacific Place in Admiralty, Hong Kong
best_for: Design lovers who want a calm, residential feel in the city
Travelers who want harbour or city views and an Admiralty base near Hong Kong Park

facts.text: Upper House was conceived by architect Andre Fu as a tranquil, residential retreat high above Pacific Place.
Natural limestone, warm timber and an understated palette carry through the hotel.
Upper House is a design-led luxury hotel in Admiralty, Hong Kong.
The hotel sits directly above Pacific Place mall, with Hong Kong Park at the door.
The interiors balance understated Japanese influences with harbour, city and mountain views.
The wellness programme includes spa and in-room treatments, curated wellness residencies, collaborations with leading experts and dedicated quiet spaces.
Rather than a conventional spa, the hotel takes a personal approach to wellness.
Check-in happens in the guest's room, where the how-tos are explained.
The hotel has easy access to the MTR.
Salisterra, on the 49th floor, serves Mediterranean-inspired cuisine.
The Green Room, next to Salisterra, serves cocktails with panoramic views.

highlights.text: Every room opens to sweeping views of Victoria Harbour or the city.
Rotating wellness residencies range from sound baths and guided meditation to yoga and longevity-focused therapies.
In the Upper Suite, wrap-around windows frame views of Victoria Harbour and the surrounding hills, with cushioned window seats and a very large tub.
The Lawn is a tucked-away garden oasis serving light bites and drinks.
Hong Kong Park, with its aviary and tea museum, is next door, and trams to The Peak or downtown are a short stroll away.

considerations.text: The hotel has no pool and no conventional full-service spa; wellness centres on in-room treatments and residencies.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning.
